messages:
From: Maya Patel <maya@novumai.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 17 Apr 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity: guidance on H100/A100/L4 for our inference mix

Hi Marcus,

Thanks again for the product walkthrough yesterday — super helpful. We're starting to formalize requirements for a dedicated capacity contract and I wanted your team's recommendation on GPU SKU mix for our primary inference workloads. High-level:

- Models: 70B LLM (quantized, long context up to 32k), several 13B/30B variants for chat, and emb/rerank endpoints for search.
- Traffic shape: steady baseline for embeddings (~30% of total calls), spiky chat traffic (peak bursts ~3x baseline), RLHF style reranks occasional.
- Constraint: procurement prefers at least 60% reserved capacity with 40% burstable. Budget-conscious but SLA-sensitive: 99.9% availability for chat.

Can you outline tradeoffs between H100, A100, and L4 for this mix (memory, perf, eviction risk, cost per token) and a starting reserve/burst split recommendation? I've attached a short workload summary.

Appreciate it — if you can get a short recommendation back this week that will help our procurement timeline.

Best,
Maya
NovumAI

Attachments: workload_summary.pdf (pdf, 260KB)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Patel <maya@novumai.com>
Cc: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 17 Apr 2025 11:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: guidance on H100/A100/L4 for our inference mix

Hi Maya — thanks for the clear brief and the attachment. Short version up front: a hybrid pool provides the best balance for your workload. Below is a concise recommendation and the rationale. I'll follow up with Jasmine and Irene to translate this into a Mutual Action Plan and a reserve/burst sizing table.

Recommendation (starter mix, reserve-focused):
- H100 (memory-first) — reserved: 18% of baseline capacity. Role: host 70B long-context quantized models and any persistent large KV-cache instances. Rationale: H100 gives headroom for large KV caches and performs best for very long context; avoids OOMs during peaks.
- A100 (throughput/price balance) — reserved: 42% of baseline. Role: chat-heavy 13B/30B models at medium context and batched generation. Rationale: A100 is cost-efficient for batch throughput and fits most 30B workloads without excessive memory risk.
- L4 (cost-efficient, scaled-out) — reserved: 0–10% (embeddings primarily in burst tier), burstable: up to 30% of peak. Role: high-concurrency embedding and lightweight rerank endpoints. Rationale: L4s are lowest unit cost and good for many small requests; not suitable for 70B or heavy KV-cache.

Practical tradeoffs and numbers (ballpark):
- Memory: H100 (80–96GB HBM usable depending on instance) comfortably hosts quantized 70B with KV cache; A100 (40–80GB variants) handles 13–30B with careful tiling; L4 (~24GB equivalent on inference) works for 7B–13B fast paths and embeddings.
- Latency/throughput: For 70B generation at 4k context, H100 ~12–18 tokens/s (single request, depending on quant). A100 for 30B models at 2k context can hit 40–80 tokens/s when batched. L4 excels at sub-100ms embedding latencies at scale.
- Cost per token: L4 << A100 < H100 (for simple tokens). But for 70B the H100 avoids repeated fallbacks and double-inference which can make it cheaper end-to-end.
- Eviction/headroom: reserve capacity should include 15–20% headroom on H100 slots to avoid OOMs from KV growth; for A100 include 10% to allow autoscaling smoothing.

Suggested reserve/burst policy: aim for 60% of steady-state capacity in reserved A100/H100 (split as above), with a 40% burst pool primarily backed by on-demand A100 and large L4 fleet for embeddings. Keep L4 mostly in burst unless you have predictable embedding volume.

Next steps (mutual action plan draft):
1) Redwood to produce an ops-sided capacity table with instance counts, estimated tokens/sec, and cost delta (Marcus/Jasmine) — ETA 2 business days.
2) NovumAI to confirm peak:baseline ratios and approve reserve % target (Maya).
3) Redwood to produce a simple proposal with reserve pricing and burst assumptions for procurement (Irene).

I've attached a one-pager that summarizes the tradeoffs and an estimated reserve-to-burst sketch. Let us know any constraints (e.g., data residency, KMS) that change the recommendations.

Thanks — happy to hop on a 30m call if you'd prefer to walk through numbers.

—Marcus
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference

Attachments: h100_a100_l4_tradeoff_onepager.pdf (pdf, 180KB)

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 18 Apr 2025 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Dedicated GPU mix recommendation and reserve/burst sizing for NovumAI

Marcus / Irene — forwarding my quick ops notes after reading Maya's workload and your reply. I'm annotating the things ops will want to lock before we publish a proposal. Keep these as checklist items for the mutual action plan.

- Workload profiling: request 48h percentiles for tokens-per-second per endpoint (p50/p95/p99) + distribution of context lengths. This drives tiling and concurrency assumptions.
- KV cache sizing: for 70B long context, reserve H100 nodes should reserve an extra 20% RAM for KV growth during multistep dialogue.
- Autoscale smoothing: set scale-up short (30–45s) and scale-down longer (3–5m) to avoid thrash on chat spikes; bursting should first allocate on-demand A100, then fall back to L4 for embeddings-only traffic.
- Fallback policy: when H100 pool saturated, we should fail-fast for long-context requests and proxy to 30B with a warning (avoid silent double-infer). That preserves SLA for chat.
- Eviction and preemption: define eviction order: ephemeral L4 -> A100 burst -> A100 reserved -> H100 reserved (do not evict H100 reserved for 70B unless explicitly approved).
- Acceptance test: run a 24h soak with synthetic p95 spikes (3x baseline) and check for <1% 5xxs and median latency within target.

I created a short mutual_action_plan.docx (stub) that maps owners and dates; suggest we include a row for procurement pricing variants (60/40, 70/30, 50/50) so NovumAI can choose.

I'll draft the capacity table next (instance counts and expected token throughput) and attach to the proposal.

—Jasmine
Solutions Engineering

Attachments: mutual_action_plan.docx (docx, 45KB)
